rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Tasks 4 Game End Overview Be the first to place all your tokens on the frame tiles in your display by fulfilling the objectives on the tiles. Turn One player takes the bag and draws tiles equal to the number of players +1 (so 5 in a 4 player game). That player then selects one tile from those available and places it orthogonally adjacent to those in their display. In clockwise order, the other players do the same. When it comes to the final tile, the bag drawer takes this one too. Then the bag is passed on for a new bag drawer. Tasks Tiles are made up of objectives (number in circle) and frames (border). The objectives tell you how many frames of what colour need to be in a contiguous group touching that tile. Some tiles may have frames that help satisfy their own objective (e.g., a tile with objective "3 green with 1 green frame" next to a tile with "2 green frames and no objectives") which satisfies the objective of 3 green frames. Once an objective has been met, cover the objective with one of your tokens. Use all your tokens to win. There are four types of objectives: One type requires a number of a single colour frame. Another requires a combo of two colours in any amount equaling the total. Another gives an OPTION of two colours, but only ONE can be used to complete. The final type requires one objective to be completed before the other, shown by an arrow. Game End The game can end immediately if a player places their final token on an objective and wins! Alternatively, if the final tiles are drawn and no one has achieved this yet, after this round the player with the most completed objectives wins.

[Rating: 3/10] Mag die ganze Reihe nicht von Nova Luna, Sagani zu Framework. Nur Patchwork bleibt. Aber trotzdem probiere ich sehr gerne alle Rosenberg Spiele!

[Rating: 3/10] Bland and overly tactical take-n-place game from a designer that should know better.

[Rating: 3/10] Fundamentally the same as Nova Luna and Sagani, but it looks worse, the colors and iconography are harder to read and it just feels like a more mediocre version of a great game.

[Rating: 4/10] More streamlined and slightly less interesting version of Nova Luna which is already an okay version of Sagani which is a worst version of Habitats. Probably the most approachable version of any of these games, but I think the theme of Habitats makes it more approachable for me and the people I play games with. The art design in this is horrible and boring to the point where I am lowering the rating by 1 just for that.  I also don't like this weird throw spaghetti at the wall thing Uwe is doing with this mechanic.

[Rating: 4/10] I'm feeling harsh on gratuitous games these days. This isn't meaningfully less good than Habitats or Nova Luna, and those games are okay. But it hardly needs to exist separately from them.  [1 play]

[Rating: 4/10] A clear downgrade from Nova Luna. I don't understand why this game was made. Way more random, less strategy. Takes longer to play.

[Rating: 4/10] Dry and relatively uninteresting tile laying game with very little to hold my interest. I'd much rather play [boardgame=357563][/boardgame]

[Rating: 4/10] Not a lot of fun in this one. Tiles are too random which makes what is supposed to be a tactical game mostly come down to luck. Edit: Down from 5 to 4. The more I play, the less I like it. Just too random the way the tiles come out and are drafted.

[Rating: 4/10] Gdyby nie istniała Nova Luna to moooże Framework bardziej by mi się spodobało. Za samą Novą Luną też nie przepadam, a Framework to jest właściwie to samo, tylko ze zmienionymi kafelkami i z jednym innym warunkiem punktacji. Wynudziłam się grając w to. No fun.  Ocena po 1 partii w 2 osoby. Czas gry = 11 minut na bga.

[Rating: 4/10] --Mar2025-- Seemed ludicrously random on this first exposure.  Perhaps it isn't - and that becomes apparent after a bunch of plays.  Not likely gonna happen, unless a friend really likes this and wants me to fill out a table.

[Rating: 4/10] Another personal tableau tile placing, racing to place all your tokens, with some potential for hate drafting.  The picture on the box is a lie, since you will not actually be creating interlocking threads like depicted, and the end result doesn't look pretty.  The solo game is a boring puzzle. Makes me want to play the Very Clever Pipe Game that came out nearly 30 years before.

[Rating: 4.9/10] abstract puzzle game follow-up to "Nova Luna" and "Sagani"  don't like looks and mechanics

[Rating: 5/10] Framework is a two-player take-and-make game.  Each turn, three tiles are drawn and divided up.  Tiles feature scoring badge(s) in different colours and/or links in those colours.  Orthogonally link as many of the right coloured links as a badge requires and place a piece on it.  The first player to run out of pieces wins.  A simple, no-interaction puzzle game that failed to engage me.  At least it is quickly over.  The tiles are reasonably thick.  The artwork is drab and the reds and browns can be difficult to distinguish in less than perfect light.

[Rating: 5/10] 2024-02-15  Initial Rating: 5.0 (February 2024)  • I always want to play Uwe Rosenberg's games no matter what. On the other hand, I tend to dislike his lighter games AND, Framework being a reworking of Nova Luna, didn't intrigue me that much.  • Framework's rules are very easy to teach. You can do it in under 2 minutes. Playtime is around 45 minutes.  • Framework is a fast-paced abstract game with gameplay very reminiscent of Nova Luna and Sagani (obviously!).
